title: Michael Chertoff's Signed Reporty Advisory Agreement: Terms Without a Payout Trail
scope: Source-bound reading of the executed March 2016 Reporty–Michael Chertoff advisory-board agreement and the bounded corpus negatives around actual contingent compensation or customer/investor referral outcomes.

sources.supports: Executed three-page advisory-board agreement; personal advisor identity; services; Approved Target mechanism; option and contingent compensation formulas; handwritten 'personally' change; District of Columbia law; Chertoff and Amir Elichai signatures.
sources.limit: Agreement proves the contractual framework, not actual target approvals, option issuance, commissions, referral payouts or customer-access outcomes.

sources.supports: Chronology and negative search: no recovered Approved Target annexes, option-grant record, compensation payment trail, Chertoff Group corporate contract, named introducer, or first-U.S.-deployment referral chain.
sources.limit: Archive-created synthesis; negative findings are limited to the searched corpus and are not universal nonexistence claims.

sources.record: White House archived Michael Chertoff biography
sources.supports: Official historical identification of Chertoff as the second U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security, sworn in February 15, 2005.
sources.limit: Role context only; does not bear on performance under the 2016 private advisory agreement.

open_questions: Whether any Approved Target annexes survive outside the recovered corpus.
Whether Reporty's board formally approved and issued the option grant described in the agreement.
Whether any invoices or payments were made under the 7.5%, 2.5%, or quarterly compensation provisions.
Who first introduced Michael Chertoff to Reporty.
Whether any later Reporty/Carbyne customer or investor was contractually credited to Chertoff.
not_established: Actual payment of the contract's contingent compensation formulas.
Actual issuance of the maximum stated options.
Government endorsement, favoritism, procurement influence or improper access.
A Chertoff-attributable causal chain to later U.S. deployments.
A corporate Chertoff Group contract with Reporty.
